title: Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident
summary: After the magnitude 9.0 Great East Japan Earthquake on 11 March 2011, a tsunami of about 15 metres reached the Fukushima Daiichi plant, cutting power and cooling. Reactor fuel melted in several units, and the accident was later rated level 7 on the INES scale. Over 100,000 people were evacuated; no deaths were attributed to radiation, while 2313 disaster-related evacuee deaths were identified by September 2020.

uncertainty.note: Earthquake at 2:46 pm on 11 March 2011; tsunami first wave 3:42 pm.

where.modern_name: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant, Ōkuma, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan
where.historical_name: Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan

importance.justification: The worst nuclear plant emergency since Chernobyl, rated INES level 7, with long-running evacuation and decommissioning consequences.

audience_note: Concerns a nuclear accident with mass evacuation and displacement, and a wider earthquake and tsunami that killed many thousands.

sources.title: Consequences of the Fukushima nuclear accident (summary of IAEA report)
GeoNames: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant

reviewer_note: The sources differ on the number of units with core damage (WNA says units 1-3; GreenFacts quoting IAEA says two units), so the summary says several units. Evacuee figures also differ (over 100,000 vs some 160,000); I give the lower figure. WNA is an industry body.
